title: Comparing Optimization Targets for Contrast-Consistent Search

en.text: Large language models keep getting more capable, yet they still state falsehoods with complete confidence. One appealing way to catch this is to read the model's own internal sense of truth: if a model somehow "knows" whether a statement is true or false, perhaps we can extract that judgment directly from its activations. Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS) is a probe built on exactly this idea. It uses no labels at all, relying only on a single constraint, that a statement and its negation must give opposite verdicts, to find a direction in activation space that separates "true" from "false."

CCS works surprisingly well, but a basic question had gone unanswered: what does its loss function actually optimize for? Without a clear answer, the probe is hard to trust and hard to improve. This NeurIPS 2023 paper, by Hugo Fry, Seamus Fallows, Ian Fan, Jamie Wright, and Nandi Schoots (Independent, Oxford University, and King's College London), opens up the CCS loss. It first corrects two long-standing misconceptions, then offers a cleaner account of the optimization target, and turns that account into a new loss function called Midpoint-Displacement (MD).

The conclusion is clean. Tune one hyper-parameter of MD to imitate CCS, and the probe directions it finds almost coincide with real CCS probes. Tune that same hyper-parameter toward accuracy, and it beats CCS. In other words, CCS succeeds not because of the particular shape of its loss formula, but because of the displacement information carried by its contrast-pair training data.
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.00488　　Code: https://github.com/ash-ai-safety-hub/g3-nandi
Two misconceptions, corrected

Before explaining CCS, the authors dispel two common but misleading descriptions of it. The first is the idea that CCS learns a separating hyperplane, splitting the true and false clusters onto opposite sides like an ordinary linear classifier. In fact, CCS classifies using only the displacement vector between a statement and its negation, projected onto the probe direction, a quantity that is invariant to translating all activations together. As Figure 1 shows, the raw activations are not cleanly separable by any hyperplane, yet CCS still works, because it reads the difference within each contrast pair rather than which side of a plane a point lands on.

en.caption: Figure 1: T5-base activations on BoolQ. The x-axis is the projection onto the first principal component; the y-axis is the projection onto the CCS direction θ̂. Red points are 'true', blue are 'false', and the black line marks where CCS outputs 0.5. True and false separate along the CCS direction (vertical axis), yet no clean separating hyperplane splits the two classes.

en.text: The second misconception is to treat CCS outputs as calibrated "truth probabilities" and to assume the probe must push those probabilities toward 0 and 1 to succeed. Figure 2 refutes this. On the same UnifiedQA T5-Large model, the encoder's CCS outputs pile up confidently at 0 and 1, yet its test accuracy is only 0.523; the decoder's outputs cluster near 0.5, looking far less confident, yet reach 0.978 accuracy. How polarized the probabilities are and how accurate the probe is turn out to be two entirely different things.

en.caption: Figure 2: histograms of CCS prober outputs for UnifiedQA T5-Large on BoolQ. (a) The encoder is highly confident, with outputs concentrated at 0 and 1, but reaches only 0.523 test accuracy; (b) the decoder's outputs cluster near 0.5 and look unconfident, yet reach 0.978 accuracy. Confidence and accuracy are decoupled.

en.text: What CCS really optimizes: a displacement-midpoint trade-off

The authors describe CCS with two simple statistics measured along the probe direction θ̂. The first is the displacement variance σ_d²: for the positive activation φ⁺ of a statement and the activation φ⁻ of its negation, the difference u = φ⁺ − φ⁻ captures how far the pair is pushed apart. The second is the midpoint variance σ_m²: the sum v = φ⁺ + φ⁻ captures how far the pair's midpoint sits from the origin.

The key observation is that the CCS loss uses a sigmoid that saturates at both ends, which forces the optimization into a trade-off: it wants to spread each pair as far apart as possible along the probe direction (maximizing σ_d²) while pulling their midpoint back toward the origin (minimizing σ_m²). The authors write this implicit trade-off out explicitly as the Midpoint-Displacement loss, L_MD = (λ − 1)·σ_d² + λ·σ_m², with λ ∈ [0, 1] and the probe direction constrained to unit norm. A single hyper-parameter λ sets the relative weight of spreading the pair versus shrinking the midpoint.

This yields two variants: MD-CCS, with λ tuned to mimic CCS, and MD-Acc, with λ tuned for accuracy. Since they differ only in λ, they form a natural ablation. As baselines, the authors also compare Mean Absolute (MA), Square Mean Root (SMR), PCA, random directions, and supervised probes, across four models and five datasets.
Results: MD is a faithful proxy for CCS

The central evidence comes from direction similarity. The weight direction learned by MD-CCS has an average cosine similarity of about 0.63 with real CCS probes. That may not sound close to 1, but two facts put it in context: CCS probes agree with each other at only 0.78, and in 1024 dimensions the probability that two random unit vectors reach a cosine similarity of 0.63 is about 10⁻²³⁷. By comparison, other equally accurate losses (MA, SMR, PCA) reach only 0.14 to 0.17 similarity with CCS. The resemblance is specific to MD, not a generic byproduct of being accurate.

On accuracy, MD-Acc averages 0.7557 test accuracy, above CCS at 0.7105, winning on three of the four models by about 4% on average. Supervised probes average 0.8674, marking the practical ceiling for these activations.

en.caption: Table 1: test accuracy of each loss function, averaged over five datasets. MD-Acc beats CCS on three of four models, by about 4% on average.
Table 2: average cosine similarity between each loss function's direction and 20 CCS probers. Only MD-CCS approaches the CCS self-similarity of 0.78; other high-accuracy losses reach just 0.14-0.17.

en.text: Ablating λ: the trade-off defines the target

Because MD-CCS and MD-Acc differ only in λ, they give a clean ablation. Tuned to mimic CCS, the direction reaches an average cosine similarity of about 0.63; tuned for accuracy, that similarity drops to about 0.38. This shows that the trade-off between σ_d² and σ_m² is the knob that defines what CCS is optimizing. Swapping MD-CCS's λ for the accuracy-tuned value raises average test accuracy from 0.7178 to 0.7557. The λ that matches CCS also barely changes across datasets and models, suggesting the identified proxy target is robust.
Takeaways and limitations

This work turns a probe that "just works" into one we can explain: CCS succeeds because of the displacement information in its contrast-pair data, the difference between a statement and its negation, not because of the specific shape of its loss formula. A simple Midpoint-Displacement loss reproduces CCS faithfully and, once retuned, outperforms it. For researchers working on interpretability and truth probing, the implication is that the exact loss formula is largely interchangeable among high-accuracy probes; the real lever is the trade-off between how far pairs are separated and how large their midpoint grows.

A few caveats are worth noting. The account of CCS's optimization target is heuristic rather than a formal proof, the experiments span four models and five datasets, and MD-Acc does not win everywhere (CCS is slightly ahead on the UQA decoder). Even so, the displacement-midpoint trade-off offers a clear, actionable lens for understanding and improving this family of unsupervised truth probes.

CCS 出人意料地好用，但一个基础问题一直没有答案：它的损失函数究竟在优化什么？如果连这一点都说不清，我们就很难信任它，也很难改进它。这篇来自 Independent、Oxford University 与 King's College London 的 NeurIPS 2023 工作（作者 Hugo Fry、Seamus Fallows、Ian Fan、Jamie Wright、Nandi Schoots）把 CCS 的损失函数拆开来看，先纠正了两个流传已久的误解，再给出一个更干净的解释，并据此设计出一个新的损失函数 Midpoint-Displacement（MD，位移-中点损失）。
结论很直接：把 MD 的一个超参数调成模仿 CCS，它找到的探针方向和真实 CCS 探针几乎重合；把同一个超参数调向准确率，它就能反过来超过 CCS。换句话说，CCS 之所以有效，靠的不是它那个特定形式的损失公式，而是对比样本对（contrast pair）里蕴含的位移信息。
论文链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.00488　　代码：https://github.com/ash-ai-safety-hub/g3-nandi
先纠正两个误解

在解释 CCS 之前，作者指出此前对它的两种常见描述都具有误导性。第一个误解是把 CCS 想成在激活上学一个「分隔超平面」，像普通线性分类器那样把真假两簇分到超平面两侧。实际上，CCS 的分类只取决于一句话与其否定之间的位移向量（displacement）在探针方向上的投影，这个量对激活的整体平移是不变的。如图 1 所示，真假样本在原始激活里并不能被一条超平面干净地分开，CCS 依然能工作——因为它读的是「样本对之间的差」，而不是「样本落在超平面哪一侧」。

zh.caption: 图 1：T5-base 在 BoolQ 上的激活。横轴是激活在第一主成分上的投影，纵轴是激活在 CCS 方向 θ̂ 上的投影，红点为「真」、蓝点为「假」，黑色横线是 CCS 输出 0.5 的分界。真假样本沿 CCS 方向（纵轴）被分开，但整体并不存在一条能干净分开两类的分隔超平面。

zh.text: 第二个误解是把 CCS 的输出当作校准过的「真值概率」，并默认它必须把概率推向 0 和 1 两端才算成功。图 2 反驳了这一点：同一个 UnifiedQA T5-Large 模型，编码器（encoder）的 CCS 输出高度自信地堆在 0 和 1 两端，测试准确率却只有 0.523；而解码器（decoder）的输出大量聚集在 0.5 附近、看起来毫不自信，准确率反而高达 0.978。可见「概率是否两极分化」和「探针准不准」根本不是一回事。

zh.caption: 图 2：UnifiedQA T5-Large 在 BoolQ 上的 CCS 探针输出直方图。(a) 编码器：输出极度自信地集中在 0 和 1，但测试准确率仅 0.523；(b) 解码器：输出大量聚集在 0.5 附近、看似不自信，测试准确率却高达 0.978。自信程度与准确率脱钩。

zh.text: CCS 真正在优化的：位移与中点的权衡
作者提出用两个沿探针方向 θ̂ 测量的简单统计量来刻画 CCS 的行为。第一个是位移方差 σ_d²：一句话的正例激活 φ⁺ 与其否定的激活 φ⁻ 之差 u = φ⁺ − φ⁻，衡量样本对被拉开的幅度。第二个是中点方差 σ_m²：两者之和 v = φ⁺ + φ⁻，衡量样本对的中点离原点有多远。

关键观察是：CCS 的损失里用了一个两端都会饱和的 sigmoid，这迫使优化陷入一种权衡——它想把每一对样本沿探针方向尽量拉开（增大 σ_d²），同时又要把它们的中点压到接近原点（减小 σ_m²）。于是作者把这个隐含的权衡直接写成一个显式的损失函数 Midpoint-Displacement：L_MD = (λ − 1)·σ_d² + λ·σ_m²，其中 λ ∈ [0, 1]、探针方向为单位向量。一个超参数 λ 就控制了「拉开位移」与「压低中点」之间的相对权重。
由此得到两个变体：MD-CCS 把 λ 调到模仿 CCS 的取值，MD-Acc 则把 λ 调到最有利于准确率。两者唯一的区别就是这个 λ，因此它们天然构成一组对照实验。作为对照，作者还比较了 Mean Absolute（MA）、Square Mean Root（SMR）、PCA、随机方向以及有监督探针等基线，覆盖四个模型和五个数据集。
实验结果：MD 是 CCS 的忠实代理

核心证据来自方向的相似度。MD-CCS 学到的权重方向与真实 CCS 探针的平均余弦相似度约为 0.63。0.63 听上去似乎不算高，但要注意两点：其一，CCS 探针彼此之间的自相似度也只有 0.78；其二，在 1024 维空间里，两个随机单位向量达到 0.63 余弦相似度的概率约为 10⁻²³⁷。相比之下，其他同样准确的损失函数（MA、SMR、PCA）与 CCS 的余弦相似度只有 0.14 到 0.17。也就是说，这种「像 CCS」是 MD 独有的，而不是任何高准确率探针都会附带的副产品。
准确率方面，MD-Acc 的平均测试准确率为 0.7557，高于 CCS 的 0.7105，在四个模型中的三个上都更优，平均领先约 4%。有监督探针的平均准确率为 0.8674，代表了这些激活能达到的实际上限。

zh.caption: 表 1：不同损失函数的测试准确率（五个数据集平均）。MD-Acc 在四个模型中的三个上超过 CCS，平均领先约 4%。
表 2：各损失函数所得方向与 20 个 CCS 探针方向的平均余弦相似度。只有 MD-CCS 接近 CCS 自相似度（0.78），其余高准确率损失只有 0.14–0.17。

zh.text: λ 的消融：权衡决定了 CCS 的目标

由于 MD-CCS 和 MD-Acc 只在 λ 上不同，它们给出了一个干净的消融。调成模仿 CCS 时，方向的平均余弦相似度约为 0.63；调向准确率时，这一相似度就掉到约 0.38。这说明 σ_d² 与 σ_m² 之间的权衡，正是决定「CCS 在优化什么」的那个旋钮。而把 MD-CCS 的 λ 换成偏准确率的取值，平均测试准确率会从 0.7178 升到 0.7557。此外，模仿 CCS 所需的 λ 在不同数据集和模型间几乎不变，说明这个代理优化目标相当稳健。
小结与局限

这篇工作把一个「黑箱式好用」的探针方法讲清楚了：CCS 的成功来自对比样本对数据里的位移信息——也就是一句话与其否定之间的差异——而不是它那个特定形状的损失公式。一个简单的 Midpoint-Displacement 损失既能忠实复现 CCS，又能在重新调参后超过它。对做可解释性和真值探测的研究者来说，这意味着损失公式本身在高准确率探针之间是大体可以互换的，真正的杠杆是「把样本对拉开多远」与「让中点长多大」之间的权衡。
需要注意的是，论文对 CCS 优化目标的解释是启发式的，而非严格证明；实验覆盖四个模型和五个数据集，MD-Acc 也并非在每个模型上都胜出（UQA 解码器上 CCS 略高）。即便如此，「位移-中点权衡」为理解与改进这类无监督真值探针提供了一个清晰而可操作的视角。

zh.title: CCS 到底在优化什么？一个更简单的损失函数复现并超越了它
zh.subtitle: NeurIPS 2023：拆开 Contrast-Consistent Search 的损失函数，用「位移-中点」权衡给出更清晰的解释

en.caption: Figure 1: T5-base activations on BoolQ. The x-axis is the projection onto the first principal component; the y-axis is the projection onto the CCS direction θ̂. Red points are 'true', blue are 'false', and the black line marks where CCS outputs 0.5. True and false separate along the CCS direction (vertical axis), yet no clean separating hyperplane splits the two classes.

en.text: What CCS really optimizes: a displacement-midpoint trade-off

The authors describe CCS with two simple statistics measured along the probe direction θ̂. The first is the displacement variance σ_d²: for the positive activation φ⁺ of a statement and the activation φ⁻ of its negation, the difference u = φ⁺ − φ⁻ captures how far the pair is pushed apart. The second is the midpoint variance σ_m²: the sum v = φ⁺ + φ⁻ captures how far the pair's midpoint sits from the origin.

The key observation is that the CCS loss uses a sigmoid that saturates at both ends, which forces the optimization into a trade-off: it wants to spread each pair as far apart as possible along the probe direction (maximizing σ_d²) while pulling their midpoint back toward the origin (minimizing σ_m²). The authors write this implicit trade-off out explicitly as the Midpoint-Displacement loss, L_MD = (λ − 1)·σ_d² + λ·σ_m², with λ ∈ [0, 1] and the probe direction constrained to unit norm. A single hyper-parameter λ sets the relative weight of spreading the pair versus shrinking the midpoint.

This yields two variants: MD-CCS, with λ tuned to mimic CCS, and MD-Acc, with λ tuned for accuracy. Since they differ only in λ, they form a natural ablation. As baselines, the authors also compare Mean Absolute (MA), Square Mean Root (SMR), PCA, random directions, and supervised probes, across four models and five datasets.

zh.caption: 图 1：T5-base 在 BoolQ 上的激活。横轴是激活在第一主成分上的投影，纵轴是激活在 CCS 方向 θ̂ 上的投影，红点为「真」、蓝点为「假」，黑色横线是 CCS 输出 0.5 的分界。真假样本沿 CCS 方向（纵轴）被分开，但整体并不存在一条能干净分开两类的分隔超平面。

zh.text: CCS 真正在优化的：位移与中点的权衡
作者提出用两个沿探针方向 θ̂ 测量的简单统计量来刻画 CCS 的行为。第一个是位移方差 σ_d²：一句话的正例激活 φ⁺ 与其否定的激活 φ⁻ 之差 u = φ⁺ − φ⁻，衡量样本对被拉开的幅度。第二个是中点方差 σ_m²：两者之和 v = φ⁺ + φ⁻，衡量样本对的中点离原点有多远。

关键观察是：CCS 的损失里用了一个两端都会饱和的 sigmoid，这迫使优化陷入一种权衡——它想把每一对样本沿探针方向尽量拉开（增大 σ_d²），同时又要把它们的中点压到接近原点（减小 σ_m²）。于是作者把这个隐含的权衡直接写成一个显式的损失函数 Midpoint-Displacement：L_MD = (λ − 1)·σ_d² + λ·σ_m²，其中 λ ∈ [0, 1]、探针方向为单位向量。一个超参数 λ 就控制了「拉开位移」与「压低中点」之间的相对权重。
由此得到两个变体：MD-CCS 把 λ 调到模仿 CCS 的取值，MD-Acc 则把 λ 调到最有利于准确率。两者唯一的区别就是这个 λ，因此它们天然构成一组对照实验。作为对照，作者还比较了 Mean Absolute（MA）、Square Mean Root（SMR）、PCA、随机方向以及有监督探针等基线，覆盖四个模型和五个数据集。

zh.subtitle: NeurIPS 2023：拆开 Contrast-Consistent Search 的损失函数，用「位移-中点」权衡给出更清晰的解释

en.caption: Figure 1: T5-base activations on BoolQ. The x-axis is the projection onto the first principal component; the y-axis is the projection onto the CCS direction θ̂. Red points are 'true', blue are 'false', and the black line marks where CCS outputs 0.5. True and false separate along the CCS direction (vertical axis), yet no clean separating hyperplane splits the two classes.

en.text: Results: MD is a faithful proxy for CCS

The central evidence comes from direction similarity. The weight direction learned by MD-CCS has an average cosine similarity of about 0.63 with real CCS probes. That may not sound close to 1, but two facts put it in context: CCS probes agree with each other at only 0.78, and in 1024 dimensions the probability that two random unit vectors reach a cosine similarity of 0.63 is about 10⁻²³⁷. By comparison, other equally accurate losses (MA, SMR, PCA) reach only 0.14 to 0.17 similarity with CCS. The resemblance is specific to MD, not a generic byproduct of being accurate.

On accuracy, MD-Acc averages 0.7557 test accuracy, above CCS at 0.7105, winning on three of the four models by about 4% on average. Supervised probes average 0.8674, marking the practical ceiling for these activations.

Table 2: average cosine similarity between each loss function's direction and 20 CCS probers. Only MD-CCS approaches the CCS self-similarity of 0.78; other high-accuracy losses reach just 0.14-0.17.

zh.caption: 图 1：T5-base 在 BoolQ 上的激活。横轴是激活在第一主成分上的投影，纵轴是激活在 CCS 方向 θ̂ 上的投影，红点为「真」、蓝点为「假」，黑色横线是 CCS 输出 0.5 的分界。真假样本沿 CCS 方向（纵轴）被分开，但整体并不存在一条能干净分开两类的分隔超平面。

zh.text: 大模型越来越强，但它们仍然会一本正经地说错话。一个自然的想法是：既然模型内部似乎「知道」一句话是真是假，能不能直接从它的激活里把这个「真值方向」读出来？Contrast-Consistent Search（CCS）就是沿着这个思路提出的探针方法：它不需要任何标签，只依赖一个简单约束——一句话和它的否定必须给出相反的判断——就能在激活空间里找到一个方向，把「真」和「假」区分开。

CCS 出人意料地好用，但一个基础问题一直没有答案：它的损失函数究竟在优化什么？如果连这一点都说不清，我们就很难信任它，也很难改进它。这篇来自 Independent、Oxford University 与 King's College London 的 NeurIPS 2023 工作（作者 Hugo Fry、Seamus Fallows、Ian Fan、Jamie Wright、Nandi Schoots）把 CCS 的损失函数拆开来看，先纠正了两个流传已久的误解，再给出一个更干净的解释，并据此设计出一个新的损失函数 Midpoint-Displacement（MD，位移-中点损失）。
结论很直接：把 MD 的一个超参数调成模仿 CCS，它找到的探针方向和真实 CCS 探针几乎重合；把同一个超参数调向准确率，它就能反过来超过 CCS。换句话说，CCS 之所以有效，靠的不是它那个特定形式的损失公式，而是对比样本对（contrast pair）里蕴含的位移信息。
论文链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.00488　　代码：https://github.com/ash-ai-safety-hub/g3-nandi
小结与局限

这篇工作把一个「黑箱式好用」的探针方法讲清楚了：CCS 的成功来自对比样本对数据里的位移信息——也就是一句话与其否定之间的差异——而不是它那个特定形状的损失公式。一个简单的 Midpoint-Displacement 损失既能忠实复现 CCS，又能在重新调参后超过它。对做可解释性和真值探测的研究者来说，这意味着损失公式本身在高准确率探针之间是大体可以互换的，真正的杠杆是「把样本对拉开多远」与「让中点长多大」之间的权衡。
需要注意的是，论文对 CCS 优化目标的解释是启发式的，而非严格证明；实验覆盖四个模型和五个数据集，MD-Acc 也并非在每个模型上都胜出（UQA 解码器上 CCS 略高）。即便如此，「位移-中点权衡」为理解与改进这类无监督真值探针提供了一个清晰而可操作的视角。

en.text: Large language models keep getting more capable, yet they still state falsehoods with complete confidence. One appealing way to catch this is to read the model's own internal sense of truth: if a model somehow "knows" whether a statement is true or false, perhaps we can extract that judgment directly from its activations. Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS) is a probe built on exactly this idea. It uses no labels at all, relying only on a single constraint, that a statement and its negation must give opposite verdicts, to find a direction in activation space that separates "true" from "false."

CCS works surprisingly well, but a basic question had gone unanswered: what does its loss function actually optimize for? Without a clear answer, the probe is hard to trust and hard to improve. This NeurIPS 2023 paper, by Hugo Fry, Seamus Fallows, Ian Fan, Jamie Wright, and Nandi Schoots (Independent, Oxford University, and King's College London), opens up the CCS loss. It first corrects two long-standing misconceptions, then offers a cleaner account of the optimization target, and turns that account into a new loss function called Midpoint-Displacement (MD).

The conclusion is clean. Tune one hyper-parameter of MD to imitate CCS, and the probe directions it finds almost coincide with real CCS probes. Tune that same hyper-parameter toward accuracy, and it beats CCS. In other words, CCS succeeds not because of the particular shape of its loss formula, but because of the displacement information carried by its contrast-pair training data.

By comparison, other equally accurate losses (MA, SMR, PCA) reach only 0.14 to 0.17 similarity with CCS. The resemblance is specific to MD, not a generic byproduct of being accurate.

On accuracy, MD-Acc averages 0.7557 test accuracy, above CCS at 0.7105, winning on three of the four models by about 4% on average. Supervised probes average 0.8674, marking the practical ceiling for these activations.

zh.caption: 图 1：T5-base 在 BoolQ 上的激活。横轴是激活在第一主成分上的投影，纵轴是激活在 CCS 方向 θ̂ 上的投影，红点为「真」、蓝点为「假」，黑色横线是 CCS 输出 0.5 的分界。真假样本沿 CCS 方向（纵轴）被分开，但整体并不存在一条能干净分开两类的分隔超平面。

zh.text: λ 的消融：权衡决定了 CCS 的目标

由于 MD-CCS 和 MD-Acc 只在 λ 上不同，它们给出了一个干净的消融。调成模仿 CCS 时，方向的平均余弦相似度约为 0.63；调向准确率时，这一相似度就掉到约 0.38。这说明 σ_d² 与 σ_m² 之间的权衡，正是决定「CCS 在优化什么」的那个旋钮。而把 MD-CCS 的 λ 换成偏准确率的取值，平均测试准确率会从 0.7178 升到 0.7557。此外，模仿 CCS 所需的 λ 在不同数据集和模型间几乎不变，说明这个代理优化目标相当稳健。

en.text: Results: MD is a faithful proxy for CCS

The central evidence comes from direction similarity. The weight direction learned by MD-CCS has an average cosine similarity of about 0.63 with real CCS probes. That may not sound close to 1, but two facts put it in context: CCS probes agree with each other at only 0.78, and in 1024 dimensions the probability that two random unit vectors reach a cosine similarity of 0.63 is about 10⁻²³⁷. By comparison, other equally accurate losses (MA, SMR, PCA) reach only 0.14 to 0.17 similarity with CCS. The resemblance is specific to MD, not a generic byproduct of being accurate.

On accuracy, MD-Acc averages 0.7557 test accuracy, above CCS at 0.7105, winning on three of the four models by about 4% on average. Supervised probes average 0.8674, marking the practical ceiling for these activations.

zh.text: 实验结果：MD 是 CCS 的忠实代理

核心证据来自方向的相似度。MD-CCS 学到的权重方向与真实 CCS 探针的平均余弦相似度约为 0.63。0.63 听上去似乎不算高，但要注意两点：其一，CCS 探针彼此之间的自相似度也只有 0.78；其二，在 1024 维空间里，两个随机单位向量达到 0.63 余弦相似度的概率约为 10⁻²³⁷。相比之下，其他同样准确的损失函数（MA、SMR、PCA）与 CCS 的余弦相似度只有 0.14 到 0.17。也就是说，这种「像 CCS」是 MD 独有的，而不是任何高准确率探针都会附带的副产品。
准确率方面，MD-Acc 的平均测试准确率为 0.7557，高于 CCS 的 0.7105，在四个模型中的三个上都更优，平均领先约 4%。有监督探针的平均准确率为 0.8674，代表了这些激活能达到的实际上限。

zh.title: CCS 到底在优化什么？一个更简单的损失函数复现并超越了它
zh.subtitle: NeurIPS 2023：拆开 Contrast-Consistent Search 的损失函数，用「位移-中点」权衡给出更清晰的解释

en.caption: Figure 1: T5-base activations on BoolQ. The x-axis is the projection onto the first principal component; the y-axis is the projection onto the CCS direction θ̂. Red points are 'true', blue are 'false', and the black line marks where CCS outputs 0.5. True and false separate along the CCS direction (vertical axis), yet no clean separating hyperplane splits the two classes.

en.text: Large language models keep getting more capable, yet they still state falsehoods with complete confidence. One appealing way to catch this is to read the model's own internal sense of truth: if a model somehow "knows" whether a statement is true or false, perhaps we can extract that judgment directly from its activations. Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS) is a probe built on exactly this idea. It uses no labels at all, relying only on a single constraint, that a statement and its negation must give opposite verdicts, to find a direction in activation space that separates "true" from "false."

CCS works surprisingly well, but a basic question had gone unanswered: what does its loss function actually optimize for? Without a clear answer, the probe is hard to trust and hard to improve. This NeurIPS 2023 paper, by Hugo Fry, Seamus Fallows, Ian Fan, Jamie Wright, and Nandi Schoots (Independent, Oxford University, and King's College London), opens up the CCS loss. It first corrects two long-standing misconceptions, then offers a cleaner account of the optimization target, and turns that account into a new loss function called Midpoint-Displacement (MD).

The conclusion is clean. Tune one hyper-parameter of MD to imitate CCS, and the probe directions it finds almost coincide with real CCS probes. Tune that same hyper-parameter toward accuracy, and it beats CCS. In other words, CCS succeeds not because of the particular shape of its loss formula, but because of the displacement information carried by its contrast-pair training data.
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.00488　　Code: https://github.com/ash-ai-safety-hub/g3-nandi
Takeaways and limitations

This work turns a probe that "just works" into one we can explain: CCS succeeds because of the displacement information in its contrast-pair data, the difference between a statement and its negation, not because of the specific shape of its loss formula. A simple Midpoint-Displacement loss reproduces CCS faithfully and, once retuned, outperforms it. For researchers working on interpretability and truth probing, the implication is that the exact loss formula is largely interchangeable among high-accuracy probes; the real lever is the trade-off between how far pairs are separated and how large their midpoint grows.

A few caveats are worth noting. The account of CCS's optimization target is heuristic rather than a formal proof, the experiments span four models and five datasets, and MD-Acc does not win everywhere (CCS is slightly ahead on the UQA decoder). Even so, the displacement-midpoint trade-off offers a clear, actionable lens for understanding and improving this family of unsupervised truth probes.

zh.text: 大模型越来越强，但它们仍然会一本正经地说错话。一个自然的想法是：既然模型内部似乎「知道」一句话是真是假，能不能直接从它的激活里把这个「真值方向」读出来？Contrast-Consistent Search（CCS）就是沿着这个思路提出的探针方法：它不需要任何标签，只依赖一个简单约束——一句话和它的否定必须给出相反的判断——就能在激活空间里找到一个方向，把「真」和「假」区分开。

CCS 出人意料地好用，但一个基础问题一直没有答案：它的损失函数究竟在优化什么？如果连这一点都说不清，我们就很难信任它，也很难改进它。这篇来自 Independent、Oxford University 与 King's College London 的 NeurIPS 2023 工作（作者 Hugo Fry、Seamus Fallows、Ian Fan、Jamie Wright、Nandi Schoots）把 CCS 的损失函数拆开来看，先纠正了两个流传已久的误解，再给出一个更干净的解释，并据此设计出一个新的损失函数 Midpoint-Displacement（MD，位移-中点损失）。
结论很直接：把 MD 的一个超参数调成模仿 CCS，它找到的探针方向和真实 CCS 探针几乎重合；把同一个超参数调向准确率，它就能反过来超过 CCS。换句话说，CCS 之所以有效，靠的不是它那个特定形式的损失公式，而是对比样本对（contrast pair）里蕴含的位移信息。
